title: Lyric Voices — Composer
subtitle: Direction happens before you write.
buildNote: Michael co-founded Lyric and built significant portions of the product directly using AI tools. This is both a case study and a build.
shortDescription: An ethical AI voice platform built on real artist partnerships. Five voices, fifteen tonal directions. Composed, not cloned.
challenge: AI voice tools optimize for realism but not for performance. Creators have no craft layer — no way to direct a voice the way a director directs a take. And most platforms are built on scraped data and unclear ethics.
insight: Output is not the same as performance. Direction has to happen before you write — not after. The intent you set shapes everything that follows.
approach: Built the Composer around a three-step model: choose the character (voice), set the intent (tonal direction), then write and direct inline. Designed the Edition system to release voices in curated, finite collections built with real professional artists under licensing and revenue-sharing agreements.
outcome: Live product with Creator ($29/mo), Studio ($99/mo), and Enterprise tiers. Edition 01 ships five voices with three tonal variants each. Edition 02 in development.
reflection: The hardest design problem wasn't the interface — it was making 'direction' feel real and intuitive before a single word is written. Inline emotion marks were the breakthrough: they give writers a way to shape a performance mid-script without switching context.

title: AI Agent Skill Doc Generator
subtitle: Engineering was writing the design artifact. Now designers can.
shareableNote: Not proprietary to AppFolio. Applicable anywhere a designer is contributing to an AI agent's orchestration layer.
problem: AppFolio designers were building AI agents that required a skill — an orchestration and execution layer that activates when the agent is triggered. To ship the skill, Engineering needed a design exemplar doc precise enough to incorporate into the master system prompt. None of the designers had experience writing this artifact. Engineering was writing it instead, removing design intent from the thing that most directly shapes how the agent behaves.
whatWasBuilt: A Claude skill that designers open in Claude Code. It walks them through a guided conversation, asking the questions necessary to produce a complete exemplar doc ready for engineering handoff. The skill educates along the way — explaining what the orchestration layer is, why each piece of the document matters, and how their design decisions will directly influence agent behavior.
outcome: Designers at AppFolio can now produce the exemplar doc themselves — with understanding, not just a filled-in template. Engineering receives a design-authored artifact. The handoff is cleaner and the agent behavior is more intentional.
whyItMatters: Any designer contributing the UX layer to an AI agent's orchestration skill faces this same gap. The skill is domain-agnostic and reusable. It represents a broader pattern in Michael's work: identifying where design intent is being lost in the AI build process and building the tool that puts it back.

title: Alexa+ Enterprise — Hospitality AI Agent
subtitle: Designing how GenAI makes a stay feel human.
shortDescription: Led design of how GenAI could make hotel and cruise stays feel more personal and human — from LLM guest scenarios to partner-facing story demonstrations.

outcome: Working experience guiding guests through real moments — booking tables, planning excursions, unwinding — across hospitality verticals.
